title: regional-sku-match-bank-splitter-bom-2027
content:
Purpose:
Provide a compact, scenario-driven capacity calculator and BOM estimator that maps model SKUs and workload topologies to regionally-sliced hardware banks (reserved vs spot), with explicit tail-latency margins and cold-spare banking per region. This is a working spreadsheet-like design intended for planning Private/VPC deployments where customers want a mix of cost efficiency and predictable latency.

Executive summary:
- Approach: match model families (base, instruction-tuned, chat) to optimized GPU SKUs and quantization levels, then slice capacity into independent region banks. Each bank has: active lanes (SLO-backed), burst lanes (best-effort), and warm spares (cold-start mitigation).
- Optimization knobs: spot/reserved ratio, quantization (fp16/int8/q4), per-request batching envelope, KV cache hit assumptions, tail-latency headroom (P95/P99 buffers).
- Output: per-region racks, GPU counts, estimated monthly cost, purchase vs reserved-commit delta, and minimal spare set for 99.9% availability given N+1 rack failure tolerance.

Inputs (cells expected):
- Region (text)
- Target throughput (tokens/sec) per region (number)
- P95 latency SLO (ms) and P99 SLO (ms)
- Average sequence length and 95th pct sequence length
- Model mix (%): base / tuned / chat / embed
- Query mix: streaming vs non-streaming (%), KV cache hit rate (%), effective batch size (tokens)
- GPU SKUs available with perf profile: GPU name, tokens/sec @ 512 seq (fp16), token-cost/hr, rack-power (kW), gpu-per-rack
- Pricing: reserved hourly, spot hourly, reserve-commit discount
- Hardware lead time and procurement multiplier for spares

Key assumptions (editable):
- 1 rack = 8 nodes, each node 8x A100-80GB equivalent for baseline calculations (adjust per SKU)
- Quantized variants provide 2.2x throughput at q4_0 relative to fp16 for chat models, 1.6x for base autoregressive models (empirical tunables)
- KV cache reduces token generation by effective 30% for chat flows with warm cache hits
- Spot availability modeled as 88% effective capacity (i.e., plan 12% additional spot capacity to meet same throughput)
- Cold-spare bank aims to cover spin-up latency within 90s window; warm spares handle sub-2s failover

Core calculation outline (spreadsheet rows):
1) Compute effective tokens/sec demand per model family = region_target_tps * model_mix_fraction * (1 - cache_hit) * avg_seq
2) Convert to GPU-hours needed: demand_tokens_sec / (gpu_tokens_sec_profile * quant_factor) => GPUs required (fractional)
3) Split GPUs into reserved_pool and spot_pool per region by spot_ratio
4) Add spares: warm_spare_percent applied to reserved_pool; cold_spare_racks appended as discrete racks by procurement multiplier
5) Map GPUs to racks (ceil up) and calculate rack-level power and rack_count
6) Compute cost: reserved_hourly*reserved_gpu_hours + spot_hourly*spot_gpu_hours + amortized-hardware-capex per-month (if purchase)
7) Produce tail-latency headroom check: if (P99_estimated > P99_SLO) => recommend increase reserved_pool by X% or reduce batch sizes

Sample table (example scenario: eu-west-1):
Columns: Region | Target tps | Model mix (base/chat/embed) | Avg seq | KV cache | GPU SKU | GPU tokens/sec @512 | Quant factor | GPUs req | Reserved GPUs | Spot GPUs | Warm spares | Cold spare racks | Racks | Monthly cost est | Notes
Row: eu-west-1 | 12000 | 40/45/15 | 256 | 0.35 | Ampere-80GB | 8500 | 2.2 (chat q4) | 18.2 | 12 | 6.2 | 2 | 1 | 3 | $38,400 | P99 ~ 210ms (SLO 250ms)
Row: us-central-1 | 24000 | 50/30/20 | 320 | 0.20 | Hopper-100GB | 15500 | 1.6 (base q4) | 24.8 | 16 | 8.8 | 3 | 1 | 4 | $70,200 | Peak-hour surge buffer suggested

Region banking notes and heuristics:
- Keep heterogenous racks grouped by SKU to reduce operator complexity. If a region must host two SKUs, prefer splitting into orthogonal banks (chat-optimized vs embed-optimized) rather than mixing nodes in same rack.
- Warm spare policy: reserve ~8-12% of reserved GPUs as 'hot pool' that can accept traffic with <2s routing change. Implement via preprovisioned VMs and container images kept running with zero-traffic attachments.
- Cold spare policy: maintain 1 discrete rack per two active racks (N+1 at rack granularity) when customer requires 99.9% SLA. Cold racks are powered off-capacity or housed in vendor-storage, with provisioning lead-time factored in.
- Spot strategy: use spot for burstable lanes and background (non-latency-critical) workloads. Target conservative spot ratio (25-40%) when P99 SLO < 300ms.

Failure and surge scenarios (quick checks):
- Rack failure: remove one rack per region and recompute remaining GPUs -> if remaining capacity < 1.0 * SLO-backed lanes => recommend cross-region failover or increase reserved ratio.
- Regional surge (2x sudden load for 15m): rely on burst lanes + cross-region routing; test if burst lanes + spot can absorb 2x for 15m with <10% P99 degradation.
- Spot reclamation: simulate 20% instant spot loss -> if reserved + warm_spares < 0.95*required_then => need additional cold spare racks or cross-region fallback.

BOM estimator output (example numeric breakdown):
- SKU: Hopper-100GB equivalent
  - Node config: 8 GPUs/node, 2 nodes/rack -> 16 GPUs/rack (example custom config)
  - Racks required (us-central-1): 4 active + 1 cold spare -> 5 racks
  - Total GPUs: 80
  - Monthly reserved cost (commit pricing): $55,000
  - Monthly spot cost (burst mix): $12,000
  - Amortized on-prem equivalent (purchase): $420,000 capex amortized @36mo -> $11,666/mo + ops

Decision guidance matrix (short):
- Low-latency (P99 < 150ms) + predictable load -> high reserved ratio (>75%), small spot fraction, more warm spares
- Cost-sensitive, bursty load -> moderate reserved (40-60%), larger spot bank, strong cold-spare planning
- Regulated / slow-provision customers -> favor purchase + on-prem racks + minimal spot

Operational checklist for handoff to SRE/procurement:
- Freeze SKU and rack power envelope (kW) -> feed to facilities for PDUs and power budget
- Confirm network uplink: per-rack 100Gbps+ recommended for KV cache heavy traffic
- Create procurement ticket with lead-time and spares: (rack_count_active + cold_spare_racks) * procurement_multiplier
- Create rollout plan for warm_spare activation script and canary traffic shaping

Open questions and TODOs (for product + infra):
- Validate quant_factor for our internal q4 pipeline on new Hopper variants (ACTION: benchmarking PR in github link)
- Formalize spot availability model using historic cloud telemetry (JIRA-DEPLOY-8721)
- Add automated spreadsheet macro to recompute rack layout given different node-per-rack constraints

Appendix: quick formulas (for copy into sheet cells)
- GPUs_required = ceil( (target_tps * avg_seq * (1-cache_hit)) / (gpu_tokens_sec * quant_factor) )
- Reserved_GPUs = round(GPUs_required * (1-spot_ratio))
- Spot_GPUs = GPUs_required - Reserved_GPUs
- Warm_spares = ceil(Reserved_GPUs * warm_spare_pct)
- Racks = ceil((Reserved_GPUs + Spot_GPUs + Warm_spares) / gpus_per_rack)

Notes for reviewers: this file is intentionally compact and prose-light to be copy-pastable into a working Google Sheet. Replace SKU and cost cells with actual vendor quotes before sending an estimate to sales.
